data.title: bn-v3b: Add MIDI conversion and source-file synth playback
data.description: Review commit 3088b3e. Focus on bounded MIDI parsing/timing, ABC voice conversion, six-channel PreviewSynth allocation, CPAL callback/device failure behavior, stdout vs stderr and exit contracts, tests, and progressive-disclosure docs.

data.body: HIGH: MIDI-to-ABC lane allocation is quadratic in allowed note count. For each note in a track/channel group, lanes.iter_mut().find scans every previously created busy lane; a valid under-16-MiB file can contain 250,000 simultaneous/retriggered notes, forcing about 31 billion lane checks before producing output. The advertised note/event caps therefore do not bound conversion time in practice. Use a per-group availability structure such as a min-heap keyed by end_tick plus stable lane index, and add a high-polyphony stress regression that demonstrates near O(notes log voices) behavior.

HIGH: Direct MIDI preview performs O(notes times tempo_changes) timing work within the documented bounds. score_from_midi calls tick_to_frame twice for every one of up to 250,000 notes, and each call linearly walks up to one million tempo changes. A legal small-enough SMF can therefore require hundreds of billions of iterations before the 10-minute render bound is even checked. Precompute cumulative elapsed time at each tempo change and binary-search ticks, or convert sorted note endpoints with one tempo sweep; add a many-tempo/many-note regression.

HIGH: cli_midi_to_abc maps every run_midi_to_abc error to exit 2 and prints usage, including a missing input file, malformed/unsupported MIDI, and output creation/write failures. Those are source/artifact failures, not CLI misuse; this violates the Bone acceptance and the command-reference convention that source failures exit 1, while music play already separates parse errors (2) from decode/device errors (1). Split argument parsing from conversion/I/O, return 2 only for invalid syntax, return 1 without usage for source/output failures, and add subprocess regressions for both classes.

MEDIUM: Even a single constant MIDI tempo is silently changed unless its microseconds-per-quarter divides 60,000,000 exactly. The converter floors integer BPM (for example 400001 us/qn becomes Q=149 instead of about 150), while the docs say gaps/note lengths are preserved and only later tempo changes warn. Slow legal tempos can incur much larger error. Round to the nearest representable BPM and emit an explicit timing-loss warning whenever conversion is inexact, or extend the ABC timing model to preserve the rational tempo; add a non-integral-tempo regression.

MEDIUM: The 16 MiB source cap is checked only with metadata before std::fs::read. A file that grows between stat/read, or a FIFO/device such as /dev/stdin whose metadata length is zero, can make music play or midi-to-abc allocate and read arbitrarily many bytes before the post-read MIDI check; ABC has no post-read length check at all. Enforce the bound while reading (take MAX+1 and reject overflow) and share that bounded reader between ABC and MIDI paths so the documented cap protects memory as well as parsing.

MEDIUM: render_score stops exactly at the last scheduled frame (or --seconds boundary), so active final notes are never note_offed and no PreviewSynth release ramp is rendered. The sample vector therefore ends at an arbitrary oscillator amplitude and CPAL immediately transitions to zero, reintroducing the end click that the documented click guard is supposed to prevent. At the render boundary, release every active channel and render enough tail samples/frames for RAMP_SAMPLES to reach silence (while keeping duration reporting explicit), with a regression asserting the final samples are silent for both natural completion and clipped previews.

LOW: The top-level SPEC command inventory now places music midi-to-abc and music play inside the sentence saying these commands operate on a cart file directly, but both consume source files and the new source-music section correctly says they neither load nor mutate a cart. The later no-RPC paragraph also explains all four commands using cart-mutation rationale, which does not apply to conversion/playback. Separate source-authoring commands from cart inspection/mutation in the inventory and give the no-RPC decision an accurate source/device/session rationale.

HIGH: ABC preview can panic on a small untrusted source instead of returning the documented decode error. Repro: pipe X:1, L:1/8, Q:1/4=120, K:C, and C/9223372036854775807 into console music play /dev/stdin --dry-run; Frac multiplication overflows at abc.rs:98 and the process exits 101. The new play path calls this unchecked rational parser directly here. Bound ABC numeric fields/durations and use checked or cross-cancelled rational arithmetic that reports a source error, then add a subprocess regression asserting exit 1 and no panic for extreme length denominators (and related cumulative-duration overflow cases).

HIGH: Multi-voice ABC preview has an input-amplification path despite the 16 MiB file cap. parse_abc_voices stores global header lines, then for every distinct voice rebuilds global.join plus that body and reparses the whole header. A legal source with a multi-megabyte T: field and thousands of small V: bodies can force gigabytes of copying/parsing from a sub-16-MiB file. Parse shared headers once and apply them to bounded voice bodies, or impose explicit header/voice/event limits and avoid cloning global text per voice; add an adversarial many-voice/large-header regression.

MEDIUM: ABC tempo changes are silently applied to the entire voice instead of at their position. parse_abc keeps only the last Q: value, and score_from_abc uses that one tempo for every event. Repro: Q:1/4=120, C, then Q:1/4=60, D dry-renders as 2.00s; correct timed playback is 1.50s. This also contradicts music-and-sfx.md, which says preview/import use the initial header tempo. Preserve tempo changes as timed events, or explicitly reject/warn and consistently use the documented initial tempo; add a two-tempo duration regression and correct the docs.

MEDIUM: CPAL stream errors can be lost at completion. The loop checks done in its condition before inspecting the shared error slot; if the data callback marks done while the error callback reports a failure, the loop exits and the fixed 150 ms tail sleep returns success without ever reading that error. Errors during the tail window are likewise ignored, violating the documented device-failure exit 1 contract. Check the error slot after observing done and again before returning (or coordinate completion/error through one state), with a callback-state unit test independent of real hardware.

Focused MIDI unit/integration tests pass, including 10k tempo changes, 20k simultaneous notes, and subprocess exit contracts.

Fixed in 196d493 and independently verified at that exact HEAD: checked/capped ABC duration parsing returns exit 1 for hostile input; shared headers are capped at 64 KiB, voices at 64, total events at 250k, and parsed without per-voice header cloning; later Q fields preserve the first tempo and warn; non-integral initial MIDI BPM rounds and warns; all source paths use a MAX+1 bounded reader; active channels receive a full silent-ending release frame; CPAL error state is checked before completion and after drain; SPEC/docs accurately separate source commands. Focused hostile-input/manual checks, music unit and integration suites, strict Clippy, reference coverage, and full just check all pass.
